composition_label: Product comparison -> Deep research -> Structured extraction

construction.implementation_origin: New implementation written directly for this isolated build; no existing implementation read or copied.

shared_schema.input: One input envelope: synthetic=true, attribute definitions, products, preferences, documents, extraction_schema.
shared_schema.output: One output envelope: status, schema_version, synthetic, comparison, research, extraction.
shared_schema.validation: The same strict recursive schema validator checks inputs and every stage boundary. Semantic validation enforces aliases, identifiers, references, unit conversions, preference compatibility, extraction type compatibility, ranks, side-by-side consistency, exact document spans, source/value correspondence and evidence/synthesis/aggregate consistency.
shared_schema.numeric_values: Finite non-boolean numbers. Numeric scalars imply canonical units; strings and {value,unit} objects support configured positive multiplicative unit conversions. Normalized values round to 12 decimal places.
shared_schema.document_grammar: A document belongs to one product; recognized claims are complete lines in attribute alias: value form. Other prose is ignored. Recognized malformed claims become unresolved questions.
shared_schema.extraction_rules: Each schema field declares id, type, required, source, optional product_id (default comparison winner), and attribute for attribute sources. Sources: name, score, attribute, summary, evidence_count, unresolved_count, has_disagreement.
shared_schema.source_spans: Document id, zero-based start, end-exclusive end, and exact quote in original decoded document text. Offsets count Python Unicode characters, not UTF-8 bytes. Derived/catalog metadata fields carry research source paths; document-backed fields also carry exact source spans.

cross_stage_handoffs.payload: Validated ranked product records, canonical attributes, preference scores, winner, and side-by-side comparison.
cross_stage_handoffs.consumption: Research processes the ranked records without reranking, aligns documentary claims to shared canonical attributes, and checks disagreement against the normalized catalog values.

cross_stage_handoffs.payload: Validated research records with inherited ranking, supported consensus values, documentary evidence spans, disputed findings, summaries, and unresolved questions.
cross_stage_handoffs.consumption: Extraction selects the research winner or an explicit product, populates schema fields from research only, and reports unsupported/disputed values as missing instead of guessing.

behavior.comparison: Weighted min-max preference scores; min/max for numbers, exact normalized match for number/text. Missing attributes score zero. Equal present values score one. Scores round to 12 decimal places; ties break by product id.
behavior.research: All matching documents contribute evidence. Repeated agreeing claims are supported, not verified truth. Documentary disagreements or catalog/document mismatches are disputed. Absent usable evidence and malformed recognized claims produce unresolved questions.
behavior.extraction: Attribute fields require undisputed documentary consensus; catalog-only values are not represented as documented facts. Required and optional missing fields are reported separately. complete depends only on required fields.
behavior.errors: CLI file, encoding, JSON, and validation errors produce one JSON object with status=error and exit 2. Successful pipeline execution prints one JSON object and exits 0, even when required extracted fields are missing.
behavior.determinism: No clock, randomness, network, subprocess providers, or model calls in implementation.
behavior.synthetic_example: Clearly labeled synthetic speakers. The top-ranked speaker has consistent price evidence, conflicting battery claims, and no mass evidence, intentionally demonstrating missing-field reporting.

excluded: Natural-language inference outside explicit claim lines

test_outcomes.cli_stdout: Exactly one parseable JSON object with status=ok; no stderr.
test_outcomes.deliverable_check: Exactly the four requested files; no cache or scratch files.
coverage: Each stage and shared output schema
Attribute aliases, text and unit normalization
Weighted ranking, ties, singleton and missing attributes
Multi-document support, disagreements and unresolved questions
Exact source spans, Unicode and CRLF
Both cross-stage handoffs and changed winner/evidence propagation
Malformed stage data, fabricated consensus and inconsistent side-by-side data
Invalid input, duplicate identifiers, unknown references, nonfinite numbers and booleans
Dimensionless values, very large weights, extreme ranges and close large integers
CLI success, usage, missing files, directory inputs, malformed JSON, duplicate JSON keys and encoding failures
